source.extractionNote: Re-extracted 2026-10-21 after designer updates. Same seven public component sets (43 variants), same node ids and keys, and the same three metadata frames (4762:6539, 4762:6735, 4762:6931); no set or frame was added or removed. Navigation Rail Item and Sub Menu Item have their own metadata frames and are specced at specs/navigation-rail-item/ and specs/sub-menu-item/. Navigation Header, Sub Menu Header, Caret Indicator and Collapsible Menu Item have no metadata of their own and are specced here under subcomponents; Caret Indicator is also used by Accordion (specs/accordion). All seven sets read in full to depth 12, every Icon instance's glyph read through its swap property, all three metadata frames re-parsed. Changes since 2026-10-20: the Navigation Rail Metadata gained a code-only Shape property and a sentence on shape inheritance in the Sub Menu Header content row; Sub Menu Header's Type=sub page now draws its back affordance as an Icon Button rather than a bare Icon, with a tighter icon-to-title gap. The master set and the other subcomponents are structurally unchanged. Updated 2026-11-20 for one change: the master set gained Show Divider (boolean, default true), which shows a vertical Divider as the root's last child in all three variants, making each 1Px wider. Variant counts of all seven sets are unchanged; the subcomponents were not re-read. Metadata re-read 2026-11-20: themes are no longer locked by default. Inverse now means the opposite shade of the page, and a new code-only Locked keeps the mode set on the component.

summary: A vertical navigation column for the edge of a desktop view, made of a narrow icon rail and a sub menu panel beside it. It is a container rather than a fixed design, three slots hold the destinations and the variant axes control only the rail's width and whether captions show. Fill the slots with Navigation Rail Item and Sub Menu Item instances. It paints no panel of its own, sitting on surface/section and marking the boundary between rail and panel with a single border.

intent.false: The narrow icon rail. Destinations read as glyphs alone unless Label is on, so it only works where the icons are genuinely recognisable.
intent.true: The wide rail, with every item's label beside its icon and the header action becoming a full Button. Reach for it when the destinations cannot be told apart by glyph. It changes the rail's overall width, so the page beside it has to give up the difference.

intent.false: Icons only in the narrow rail.
intent.true: Adds a caption under each icon in the narrow rail, buying recognition without the width of Expanded. The column stays narrow, so only very short words fit. Content placed in the Menu Slot is held separately per Label setting and does not carry across a change to it.
Shows the action under the header, a create or compose entry point rather than a destination.
intent.false: Hides it, for a rail that is purely navigational.

intent.true: Shows the last footer item, which carries the panel glyph and is how a user moves between the narrow and wide rail.
intent.false: Hides it. Only do this when something outside the rail controls Expanded, otherwise the user has no way to change it back.

intent.true: Shows the panel beside the rail, for destinations that have a second level.
intent.false: Hides the panel and leaves the icon rail on its own. The rail's overall width drops by the panel's width, so the layout beside it moves.

intent.true: Shows the Menu Slot below the three built-in rail items, which is where additional destinations go.
intent.false: Hides the slot along with everything placed in it, leaving only the three built-in items.

intent.true: Shows the Footer Slot above the fixed footer items.
intent.false: Hides the slot along with everything placed in it.

intent.true: Shows a divider down the rail's trailing edge, between the rail and the page.
intent.false: Hides it, for a rail whose neighbour already draws that edge.

controls: corner shape of every nested component: Navigation Rail Item, Sub Menu Item, Collapsible Menu Item, the header action, and the Buttons and Icon Buttons inside Navigation Header and Sub Menu Header (including the back button). The rail itself has no corners and is unaffected.

intent.rounded: Code only, not drawn in Figma. Gives everything inside the rail rounded corners (radius/sm): rail items, sub menu rows, Collapsible Menu Items, the header action, and the buttons in both headers, including back. The rail's own edges never change.
intent.sharp: Square corners (radius/none) on everything inside the rail.

shape.observed: Not a Figma property. As drawn (the rounded default), the rail's placed items and header action carry radius/element-sm, Button's Shape=rounded radius (the same value as radius/sm today).
shape.ownerDecision: Shape reaches every nested component; rounded = radius/sm, sharp = radius/none. A nested Button or Icon Button takes the same-named shape.

tokens._note: Names bound by the master and the four subcomponents specced here; the item tokens are in their own specs. All 26 bound names resolve in tokens/base; all 11 glyphs are in packages/icons/codepoints.json and not retired. animations/smooth (250ms ease-in-out, size collection) is the rail's motion by owner decision: every opening and closing in the rail, the caret included. animations/spring remains the Caret Indicator's default outside the rail. Both resolve in tokens/base/size. Theme axes from tokens/manifest.json, which now also lists extension collections (companion, target, condensed) that override some of these names per brand.

states.whatChanges: The rail has no interaction states of its own. Selection, hover, press and disabled all live on the Navigation Rail Item and Sub Menu Item instances inside the slots, so the container never changes appearance.

states.trigger: The Toggle item, or Expanded set from outside
states.whatChanges: The icon rail widens or narrows, labels appear or leave, and whatever sits beside the rail moves with it.

states.trigger: Show Sub menu, or choosing a destination with a second level
states.whatChanges: The panel opens or closes beside the rail, and the overall width follows.
The group's rows reveal or hide, and its caret turns.

behavior.description: Collapse / expand, sub menu open / close and group open / close all use animations/smooth (ease-in-out, 250ms), the caret's turn included. Turn motion off under prefers-reduced-motion.
behavior.inCode: Width (rail, panel) and height (group rows) transition once per change, never on first render. Labels and panel content keep their final layout and are clipped by the moving edge, so text never reflows or wraps mid-animation. The Caret Indicator takes smooth inside the rail through its --zds-caret-indicator-motion hook and keeps its spring elsewhere.

behavior.description: Expanded and Show Sub menu both change the component's overall width. Whatever sits beside the rail has to absorb the difference, so plan the page for every width you intend to ship.

Sub menu labels that don't fit end in an ellipsis. Hovering a cut-off label for 3 seconds shows it in full in a tooltip; keyboard focus shows it at once. Labels that fit show no tooltip, and the tooltip is not announced a second time to screen readers.
Carets turn a single glyph rather than swapping between two. Figma shows each end state with its own glyph; build one glyph that rotates, on animations/smooth inside the rail.
The menu list takes whatever height is left between the header block and the footer, so the footer stays pinned to the bottom however many items sit above it.

content.description: Additional destinations below the three built-in rail items. It ships holding a Divider and three items. See the Navigation Rail Item Metadata frame. Its content is stored separately for each Label setting, so switching Label leaves the content behind.
Destinations pinned to the bottom, above the two fixed footer items. It ships holding a Divider and three items, and the same content is shared by every variant.

content.type: slot, holds Sub Menu Item and Collapsible Menu Item
content.description: The second-level list inside the panel. It ships holding one Collapsible Menu Item and four Sub Menu Items, and its content is shared by every variant. See the Sub Menu Item Metadata frame.

The panel's title bar, carrying a back affordance, an editable title and a trailing slot of its own holding a Button. The rail leaves the instance exposed, so all of that is reachable without detaching. The shape of all sub elements are inherited from the main rail component.

The header is a Navigation Header showing an avatar. The action below it is an Icon Button in the narrow rail and a Button in the wide one. Neither is a slot, so changing them means overriding the nested instance.

do: Fill the Menu Slot and Footer Slot with Navigation Rail Item instances and let the rail handle the spacing and alignment.
Keep the toggle item visible unless something outside the rail controls Expanded, since it is the only control a user has over the rail's width.
dont: Don't place Menu Slot content and then switch Label. The two Label settings hold that slot's content separately, so the content will not come with you.
Don't lean on Label to make destinations readable. The caption sits inside the narrow column and only the shortest words fit, Expanded is the setting that gives labels room.

accessibility: The rail is a container and announces nothing itself. The destinations inside carry the meaning, so each needs a clear name even when only its glyph shows.
Collapsed, destinations are glyph-only unless Label is on. An icon is not a name, so the accessible name has to come from code.
Exactly one destination should read as selected across the rail and the panel together, and nothing in the component enforces that.
The panel is separated from the rail by a single border on its leading edge. Check that border/default reads against surface/section, because nothing else marks the boundary.
The toggle item is the only way a user changes the rail's width. Hiding it without providing another control strands anyone who needs the labels.

layoutTheming.description: The narrow rail is 72px and the wide rail 200px; Rail Max Width can cap the wide rail. The sub menu sizes to its content: as wide as its widest top-level row or its header, never narrower than 240px, and all rows share that width. A Collapsible Menu Item never makes it wider. Sub Menu Max Width can cap it. Figma draws the sub menu at a fixed 240px; build it to size to its content.
layoutTheming.inCode: Owner decision: the panel hugs its list (min 240px), so the overall width grows with the longest row.

layoutTheming.description: Fills its parent, drawn at 991px. The icon rail and the panel both fill it, and the menu list absorbs the space left between the header block and the footer.
12px on all four sides of the icon rail, space/md left and right and space/card top and bottom, with a 12px (space/md) gap between the header, the action, the menu list and the footer.
space/2xs between items in both the menu list and the footer. The Menu Slot adds space/2xs of horizontal padding of its own.
The Sub Menu Slot insets its rows by space/sm on all four sides, with a space/2xs gap between them.

A 1px border on border/default down the leading edge of the sub menu panel, and a 1px bottom border on the same token under the Sub Menu Header. Show Divider adds a 1px Divider down the rail's trailing edge.

The Nav rail inherit’s page theme or makes use of the inverse property for inverted light-dark mode fills, or can be locked to a specific light or dark mode using the lock property, in this case it’s stays in the shade mode irrespective of page’s mode (AAA switch is propagates, only the corresponding dark-light are affected) . All internal element follow the rail mode.
The rail binds only its surface and its two borders. Every other colour comes from the items in the slots.

issues.detail: Show Header (#3388:12, boolean, default true) is bound to nothing in any variant: the header always shows. It is also absent from the metadata. Either wire it or remove it.

Sub Menu Slot's preferred instance is the Sub Menu Item set 3404:28070 (key e97045ae…), an older 4-variant copy (no Nested, no active) that sits on no page. The live set is 3453:54275 (key 2ab793c0…). Collapsible Menu Item's closed variant also still holds four instances of the orphan in its hidden slot.

Menu Slot and Footer Slot prefer Divider plus a set with key a93b5504…, which is neither this page's Navigation Rail Item (7848f7c7…) nor the Tab Bar page's (356c565c…) and was not found in the library search. The metadata says these slots hold Navigation Rail Item; the picker probably offers a deleted item.

Resolved by owner decision: the rail's shape drives the items' radius, rounded = radius/sm (the item sets' own binding; radius/element-sm, which Figma rebinds placed items to, has the same value today), sharp = radius/none.
Border widths are unbound: the sub menu panel's left border and the Sub Menu Header's bottom border are raw 1Px strokes with colour border/default. Use stroke/thin (the Divider's token) in code.

In Type=sub page the back affordance (now an Icon Button, Size=small, Shape=sharp, Flavour=subtle, glyph arrow-back) is not bound to Show Leading Icon, so it cannot be hidden and the property does nothing in that variant. Unchanged by the 2026-10-21 update.
Layout & Theming says the rail's height is Fill. The component itself is drawn fixed at 991Px; fill is something the consumer sets on the instance. Build it to fill its container.
Layout & Theming says the Menu Slot adds space/xxs of horizontal padding. That is true in the narrow variants only; in the wide variant its padding is space/none.

The page records a code deviation: 'Code only supports the collapsed, icon-only rail layout (fixed 64px width). The expanded full-label mode shown in Figma is not available. Menu Slot, Footer Slot — Are not currently implemented slots in code.' Figma's narrow rail measures 72Px; the existing code is behind the design.

Collapsible Menu Item's open header fill is interactive/ghost/background/pressed with an extra paint opacity of 0.1, on a token that is already translucent; the same applies to the item scrims (see specs/navigation-rail-item and specs/sub-menu-item). Use the token alone in code.
Nothing wires the toggle item to Expanded, and nothing enforces a single selected destination across rail and panel (the metadata says so). Code owns both.

Resolved by owner decision: rounded = radius/sm, sharp = radius/none. Figma's sharp description is still copied from More Rail Items ('Hides the slot along with everything placed in it…'); the Figma text needs fixing, the behaviour does not.
issues.resolved: Fixed in the Figma metadata on 2026-10-21: the sharp row now describes square corners (radius/none).

issues.detail: Resolved by owner decision: the Sub Menu Header's back Icon Button and trailing actions, and Navigation Header's settings Icon Button, follow the rail's shape (Figma, which draws them sharp in the rounded rail, is out of date), as does the header action.

Resolved by owner decision: Shape reaches every nested component, including the header action and the header buttons. In code it is a context value (React) / a property the rail sets (web components) that the items read, and the rail forwards it to the Buttons and Icon Buttons it renders.
Menu Slot#3200:20 is bound to no layer; the live Menu Slots are #3497:69 (Label=false) and #3497:65 (Label=true). The per-Label split is a Figma workaround; in code it is one menuSlot.
Only three variants exist: Label=true with Expanded=true is not built (the wide rail always shows labels).
Unbound gaps of 10 on Navigation Header's collapsed root and on Caret Indicator's root have a single flowing child, so they never render.
Header type (avatar or logo) and Sub Menu Header type are swap-only from the rail. The rail pins Type=avatar and Type=sub page; whether they become props is the implementer's call.

Open=true puts the header row into State=active (ghost pressed scrim) for as long as the group is open, so an open group reads as pressed. It also overrides the Sub Menu Item's caret to Direction=vertical (expand-more/expand-less), where a plain Sub Menu Item uses horizontal (chevron-right).

Navigation Header, Sub Menu Header, Caret Indicator and Collapsible Menu Item have no metadata frames and no component descriptions; their API above comes from structure only. No focus states anywhere on the page.

A stray top-level frame named 'Navigation Rail' (5547:2915) holds a detached copy of the sub menu panel (Sub Menu Header instance plus a Sub Menu Slot frame); it is not a component. The 'Navigation Rail Template' frame's details card carries copy pasted from Dropdown ('The full dropdown pattern that composes a trigger with its menu…'), and three of its five instances point at a component named 'Navigation Rail/false/false' that is not this set.

The Tab Bar page has its own set named 'Navigation Rail Item' (3635:1151). It is a different component (a horizontal tab item), not a copy of this page's item; see specs/navigation-rail-item duplicateCheck. Not specced.

Caret Indicator still swaps glyphs per Open variant in Figma (expand-more/expand-less, chevron-right/expand-more). The owner decision to rotate one glyph stands: on animations/smooth inside the rail, animations/spring elsewhere. Figma has not been redrawn to rotate; its metadata now names the timing (animations/smooth), so the old 'Figma stores no timing' gap is resolved.

tokens/manifest.json now lists extension collections (companion: palette; target: primitives, palette; condensed: typography, size). The rail binds names only, so it themes under them without change, but the condensed size/typography overrides can move the measured widths recorded here.
Figma has no inverse or locked property; both are code-only. The metadata changed on 2026-11-20: the rail follows the page's mode by default, where it used to be locked to dark.

The metadata does not say which mode is a locked rail's default, or what a rail shows with both locked and inverse set. In code (2026-11-20, to confirm): a locked rail is dark, and light with inverse.

codeChanges.note: Owner decisions made after the Figma extraction. Each overrides or adds to what Figma draws; build these, not the Figma value.

properties.does: Sets the corners of everything inside the rail: rail items, sub menu rows, Collapsible Menu Items, the header action, and the buttons in both headers (including the back button). Rounded uses radius/sm, sharp uses radius/none. The rail's own edges never change.

The rail follows the page's mode. inverse shows the opposite shade instead: dark on a light page, light on a dark one. The contrast level (AA or AAA) still follows the page, and everything inside the rail follows the rail.
Keeps the rail dark, or light with inverse, whatever the page's mode. The contrast level (AA or AAA) still follows the page.

properties.values: a CSS length, or a number in px
properties.does: Caps the width of the wide rail (normally 200px). The narrow rail is not affected. Labels that no longer fit end in an ellipsis.

properties.values: a CSS length, or a number in px
properties.does: Caps the width of the sub menu. Rows that no longer fit end in an ellipsis. A cap below 240px also lowers the 240px minimum.

subMenuWidth: The sub menu sizes to its content: as wide as its widest top-level row or its header, never narrower than 240px. Figma draws it at a fixed 240px.
All rows share that one width.
A Collapsible Menu Item never makes the sub menu wider. It takes the width the other rows give it, and its labels end in an ellipsis when they don't fit.
truncatedLabels: When a sub menu label is cut off, hovering it for 3 seconds shows the full label in a tooltip. This applies to every Sub Menu Item and to Collapsible Menu Item headers.
Labels that fit show no tooltip.
Keyboard focus shows it at once.
The tooltip repeats the row's name, so it is not announced a second time to screen readers.
The tooltip follows the rail's dark or light mode.
motion: Every opening and closing in the rail uses animations/smooth (250ms, ease-in-out): the rail collapsing and expanding, the sub menu showing and hiding, and Collapsible Menu Items opening and closing.
Carets turn a single glyph rather than swapping glyphs (Figma swaps). Inside the rail they turn on animations/smooth; elsewhere Caret Indicator uses animations/spring.
Nothing animates on first render, and all motion is turned off for users who prefer reduced motion.
